response: Yes, the type of remission after a major depressive episode is an important risk factor for relapses in a 4-year follow-up. Patients who achieve full remission have a lower risk of relapse compared to those who achieve only partial remission. Additionally, the quality of remission, such as the presence of residual symptoms, can also predict the risk of relapse. Studies have shown that individuals with residual symptoms are more likely to experience a relapse within 4 years compared to those with full remission. Therefore, the type and quality of remission are significant predictors of relapse risk in the long term.
